title: BiBi-Linux Wiper Incident Response
description: Investigate and respond to the BiBi-Linux wiper malware incident affecting your network. This scenario simulates a realistic compromise lifecycle, from initial detection to forensic analysis and containment.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The BiBi-Linux wiper malware has been detected in your network. This malware is designed to corrupt files with random data, manipulate partition tables, and append mocking 'BiBi' extensions. It does not have command-and-control (C2) capabilities or lateral movement features but does exfiltrate data. The malware targets Linux systems. Your task is to investigate the incident, analyze forensic artifacts, and trace the malware's spread to contain the threat. The learning objective of this scenario is to develop your incident response and forensic analysis skills in a realistic cybersecurity environment.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have access to the workstation (192.168.50.5) as user 'cyrano' with password 'cyrano'. From this host, you can SSH to the file-server (192.168.50.6) using the same credentials. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Identify and investigate suspicious file destruction activity
levels.content: Examine the system logs and file artifacts on the workstation to identify any suspicious file destruction activity. Look for evidence of files being overwritten with random data or renamed with random hex strings. The flag is a directory path.
levels.solution: Check the system logs in /var/log/ for any unusual activity. Also, examine the contents of the /data/company_files directory for any signs of file corruption or unusual filenames.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: System logs often contain evidence of unusual activity. Start by examining the logs in the /var/log/ directory.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for any signs of file corruption or unusual filenames in the /data/company_files directory.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The flag you are looking for is the path to the directory containing corrupted files.

reference_solution.explanation: This command connects to the workstation via SSH and lists the contents of the /data/company_files directory. This directory is expected to contain evidence of file corruption or unusual filenames, which are indicative of the BiBi-Linux wiper malware's activity.

levels.title: Investigate malware execution logs and forensic artifacts
levels.content: Analyze the logs and artifacts left by the BiBi-Linux wiper malware on the workstation. Look for any logs or files that indicate the malware's execution and the extent of the damage caused. The flag is a file path.
levels.solution: Check the /var/log/disk-maintenance.log file for detailed logs of the malware's activity.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Malware often leaves logs of its activity. Start by examining the logs in the /var/log/ directory.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for detailed logs of the malware's activity in the /var/log/disk-maintenance.log file.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The flag you are looking for is the path to the log file containing detailed logs of the malware's activity.

reference_solution.explanation: This command connects to the workstation via SSH and displays the contents of the /var/log/disk-maintenance.log file. This file is expected to contain detailed logs of the BiBi-Linux wiper malware's activity, which will help in understanding the extent of the damage caused.

levels.title: Trace malware spread from one host to another
levels.content: Investigate how the BiBi-Linux wiper malware spread from the workstation to the file-server. Look for any scripts, services, or logs that indicate lateral movement activity. The flag is a file path.
levels.solution: Examine the /usr/local/bin/net-sync.sh script on the workstation for any signs of lateral movement.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Malware often spreads through scripts or services. Start by examining scripts in the /usr/local/bin/ directory.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for signs of lateral movement in the /usr/local/bin/net-sync.sh script.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint

This script is expected to contain signs of lateral movement, indicating how the BiBi-Linux wiper malware spread from the workstation to the file-server.
